newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Canadian miner confident of Busang gold reserves.
newsitem.headline: Canadian miner confident of Busang gold reserves.

text.p: The chief executive of Canadian mining firm Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Monday he was confident the calculation of gold resources contained in the Busang property in Indonesia were accurate.

Bre-X announced on February 17 that the latest estimate of reserves in the Busang find in East Kalimantan province amounted to 70.95 million ounces of gold, making it the single biggest gold discovery of the century.

"The company's board of directors has absolute confidence in the integrity and accuracy of assay results and resource calculations reported by the company for the Busang gold find since inception of exploration in 1993," Bre-X chief David Walsh said a statement from company headquarters in Calgary, Alberta.

The statement said a Bre-X technical team under the direction of vice-president John Felderhof "has arrived in Jakarta to ensure continuity of the process that will secure the expeditious development of the Busang gold deposit".
Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc, which has a 15 percent stake in Busang, is currently conducting an evaluation of the deposit known as a due diligence process before developing a mine.
Bre-X has a 45 percent stake in Busang, and Indonesian interests 40 percent.

Shares in Bre-X on the Toronto Stock Exchange fell Canadian $2.80 to a 52-week low of $14.65 on Friday after a report in the Indonesian newspaper Harian Ekonomi Neraca cast doubt on the size of the Busang deposit.

The New Orleans-based Freeport said last Friday its due diligence of the site was not completed. Indonesian Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Sunday his department would look into news about the Busang deposit.
Bre-X was also hit by the loss of its chief geologist, Filipino Michael de Guzman, who fell to his death from a helicopter on his way to the Busang property last Wednesday.

Search and rescue officials said on Monday his body had been found the day before. Indonesian officials are not discounting the possibility that de Guzman might have committed suicide as he was apparently suffering from acute hepatitis B.
The Busang property was the subject of a recent bidding war as several mining companies wooed the Indonesian government for control of the property.
